passages.text: This is the word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD: “Go down at once to the potter’s house, and there I will reveal My message to you.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Jeremiah.
The LORD gave Jeremiah a message.
The LORD said, “Get up.
Go down to the potter’s house.
When you arrive there, I will tell you My words.
I will reveal My message to you at the potter’s house.”
passages.original: הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה אֶֽל־ יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃ ק֥וּם וְיָרַדְתָּ֖ בֵּ֣ית הַיּוֹצֵ֑ר וְשָׁ֖מָּה אַשְׁמִֽיעֲךָ֥ אֶת־ דְּבָרָֽי׃

passages.text: So I went down to the potter’s house and saw him working at the wheel.
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah was a prophet of the LORD.
The LORD spoke to Jeremiah.
The LORD told Jeremiah to go to the potter’s house.
Jeremiah obeyed the LORD.
Jeremiah went down to the potter’s house.
Jeremiah saw the potter.
The potter was working.
The potter was working at the wheel.
passages.original: וָאֵרֵ֖ד בֵּ֣ית הַיּוֹצֵ֑ר וְהִנֵּהוּ עֹשֶׂ֥ה מְלָאכָ֖ה עַל־ הָאָבְנָֽיִם׃

passages.text: But the vessel that he was shaping from the clay became flawed in his hand; so he formed it into another vessel, as it seemed best for him to do.
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah saw the potter working with clay.
The potter shaped a vessel from the clay.
The vessel became flawed in the potter’s hand.
The potter did not keep the flawed vessel.
The potter made the clay into another vessel.
The potter shaped the new vessel as he thought best.
passages.original: וְנִשְׁחַ֣ת הַכְּלִ֗י אֲשֶׁ֨ר ה֥וּא עֹשֶׂ֛ה בַּחֹ֖מֶר בְּיַ֣ד הַיּוֹצֵ֑ר וְשָׁ֗ב וַֽיַּעֲשֵׂ֙הוּ֙ כְּלִ֣י אַחֵ֔ר כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר יָשַׁ֛ר בְּעֵינֵ֥י הַיּוֹצֵ֖ר לַעֲשֽׂוֹת׃פ

passages.text: Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying, “O house of Israel, declares the LORD, can I not treat you as this potter treats his clay? Just like clay in the potter’s hand, so are you in My hand, O house of Israel.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me.
He said these words.
The LORD is powerful.
He controls all things.
He spoke to the house of Israel.
He said, “I am like the potter.
You are like clay in the potter’s hand.
The potter shapes the clay as he wishes.
I can shape you, house of Israel, as I wish.
You are in My hand, house of Israel.
I have full power over you, just as the potter has power over the clay.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־ יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֽוֹר׃ הֲכַיּוֹצֵ֨ר הַזֶּ֜ה לֹא־ אוּכַ֨ל לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת לָכֶ֛ם בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֑ה הִנֵּ֤ה כַחֹ֙מֶר֙ בְּיַ֣ד הַיּוֹצֵ֔ר כֵּן־ אַתֶּ֥ם בְּיָדִ֖י בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס

passages.text: At any time I might announce that a nation or kingdom will be uprooted, torn down, and destroyed.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about nations and kingdoms.
God can decide to act at any moment.
God may say that He will uproot a nation.
God may say that He will tear down a kingdom.
God may say that He will destroy them.
passages.original: רֶ֣גַע אֲדַבֵּ֔ר עַל־ גּ֖וֹי וְעַל־ מַמְלָכָ֑ה לִנְת֥וֹשׁ וְלִנְת֖וֹץ וּֽלְהַאֲבִֽיד׃

passages.text: But if that nation I warned turns from its evil, then I will relent of the disaster I had planned to bring.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the nation.
God warns the nation about its evil.
The nation turns away from its evil.
God sees the nation change.
God decides not to bring the disaster He planned.
God relents from the harm He intended.
passages.original: וְשָׁב֙ הַגּ֣וֹי הַה֔וּא מֵרָ֣עָת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי עָלָ֑יו וְנִֽחַמְתִּי֙ עַל־ הָ֣רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר חָשַׁ֖בְתִּי לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת לֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: And if at another time I announce that I will build up and establish a nation or kingdom, and if it does evil in My sight and does not listen to My voice, then I will relent of the good I had intended for it.
passages.sermon:
God sometimes announces that He will build up a nation or a kingdom.
God sometimes says He will plant and establish that nation or kingdom.
If that nation or kingdom does evil in God's sight, God sees it.
If that nation or kingdom does not listen to God's voice, God notices it.
Then God will change His mind about the good He planned for that nation or kingdom.
God will not do the good He said He would do for them.
passages.original: וְרֶ֣גַע אֲדַבֵּ֔ר עַל־ גּ֖וֹי וְעַל־ מַמְלָכָ֑ה לִבְנֹ֖ת וְלִנְטֹֽעַ׃ וְעָשָׂ֤ה הָרָעָה בְּעֵינַ֔י לְבִלְתִּ֖י שְׁמֹ֣עַ בְּקוֹלִ֑י וְנִֽחַמְתִּי֙ עַל־ הַטּוֹבָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָמַ֖רְתִּי לְהֵיטִ֥יב אוֹתֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: Now therefore, tell the men of Judah and the residents of Jerusalem that this is what the LORD says: ‘Behold, I am planning a disaster for you and devising a plan against you. Turn now, each of you, from your evil ways, and correct your ways and deeds.’
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Jeremiah.
The LORD gave a message for the men of Judah and the people living in Jerusalem.
The LORD said, “I am planning a disaster for you.
I am making a plan against you.
Each of you must turn from your evil ways.
Change your ways.
Change your actions.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֡ה אֱמָר־ נָ֣א אֶל־ אִישׁ־ יְהוּדָה֩ וְעַל־ יוֹשְׁבֵ֨י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם לֵאמֹ֗ר כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י יוֹצֵ֤ר עֲלֵיכֶם֙ רָעָ֔ה וְחֹשֵׁ֥ב עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם מַֽחֲשָׁבָ֑ה שׁ֣וּבוּ נָ֗א אִ֚ישׁ מִדַּרְכּ֣וֹ הָֽרָעָ֔ה וְהֵיטִ֥יבוּ דַרְכֵיכֶ֖ם וּמַעַלְלֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: But they will reply, ‘It is hopeless. We will follow our own plans, and each of us will act according to the stubbornness of his evil heart.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The people of Judah and Jerusalem speak.
They say, "It is hopeless."
They refuse to listen to God.
They choose to follow their own plans.
Each person decides to act by the stubbornness of his own evil heart.
They reject God's warning.
They continue to do what is wrong.
passages.original: וְאָמְר֖וּ נוֹאָ֑שׁ כִּֽי־ אַחֲרֵ֤י מַחְשְׁבוֹתֵ֙ינוּ֙ נֵלֵ֔ךְ וְאִ֛ישׁ שְׁרִר֥וּת לִבּֽוֹ־ הָרָ֖ע נַעֲשֶֽׂה׃ס

passages.text: Therefore this is what the LORD says: “Inquire among the nations: Who has ever heard things like these? Virgin Israel has done a most terrible thing.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
The LORD says, "Ask the nations about this.
Has anyone ever heard of such things?
Virgin Israel has done a very terrible thing."
passages.original: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה שַֽׁאֲלוּ־ נָא֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם מִ֥י שָׁמַ֖ע כָּאֵ֑לֶּה שַֽׁעֲרֻרִת֙ עָשְׂתָ֣ה מְאֹ֔ד בְּתוּלַ֖ת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: Does the snow of Lebanon ever leave its rocky slopes? Or do its cool waters flowing from a distance ever run dry?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people Israel.
God compares Israel to Lebanon’s mountains.
Snow covers the rocky slopes of Lebanon.
The snow does not leave the rocks.
Cool waters flow from Lebanon’s mountains.
These waters come from far away.
These waters do not run dry.
God asks if this ever changes.
The answer is no.
Snow remains on the mountains.
The waters keep flowing.
passages.original: הֲיַעֲזֹ֥ב מִצּ֛וּר שָׂדַ֖י שֶׁ֣לֶג לְבָנ֑וֹן אִם־ יִנָּתְשׁ֗וּ מַ֛יִם זָרִ֥ים קָרִ֖ים נוֹזְלִֽים׃

passages.text: Yet My people have forgotten Me. They burn incense to worthless idols that make them stumble in their ways, leaving the ancient roads to walk on rutted bypaths instead of on the highway.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about His people Israel.
God says, "My people have forgotten Me."
They burn incense to worthless idols.
These idols cannot help them.
The people stumble in their ways because of these idols.
They leave the ancient, good paths.
They choose to walk on rough, unmarked roads instead.
They do not follow the right way.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ שְׁכֵחֻ֥נִי עַמִּ֖י לַשָּׁ֣וְא יְקַטֵּ֑רוּ וַיַּכְשִׁל֤וּם בְּדַרְכֵיהֶם֙ שְׁבִילֵ֣י עוֹלָ֔ם לָלֶ֣כֶת נְתִיב֔וֹת דֶּ֖רֶךְ לֹ֥א סְלוּלָֽה׃

passages.text: They have made their land a desolation, a perpetual object of scorn; all who pass by will be appalled and shake their heads.
passages.sermon:
The people have made their land empty and ruined.
Their land is now a place of shame forever.
Everyone who passes by the land will be shocked.
They will shake their heads in disbelief.
passages.original: לָשׂ֥וּם אַרְצָ֛ם לְשַׁמָּ֖ה שְׁרוּקַת עוֹלָ֑ם כֹּ֚ל עוֹבֵ֣ר עָלֶ֔יהָ יִשֹּׁ֖ם וְיָנִ֥יד בְּרֹאשֽׁוֹ׃

passages.text: I will scatter them before the enemy like the east wind. I will show them My back and not My face in the day of their calamity.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God says, “I will scatter My people before their enemy.
I will scatter them like the east wind scatters things.
I will turn My back to them in their time of disaster.
I will not show them My face when trouble comes.
passages.original: כְּרֽוּחַ־ קָדִ֥ים אֲפִיצֵ֖ם לִפְנֵ֣י אוֹיֵ֑ב עֹ֧רֶף וְלֹֽא־ פָנִ֛ים אֶרְאֵ֖ם בְּי֥וֹם אֵידָֽם׃ס

passages.text: Then some said, “Come, let us make plans against Jeremiah, for the law will never be lost to the priest, nor counsel to the wise, nor an oracle to the prophet. Come, let us denounce him and pay no heed to any of his words.”
passages.sermon:
Some people spoke together.
They said, "Let us make plans against Jeremiah."
Jeremiah was a prophet.
They believed the law would always remain with the priest.
They believed wise men would always have counsel.
They believed prophets would always have a message from God.
They said, "Let us attack Jeremiah with our words."
They said, "Let us not listen to anything he says."
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ לְכ֨וּ וְנַחְשְׁבָ֣ה עַֽל־ יִרְמְיָהוּ֮ מַחֲשָׁבוֹת֒ כִּי֩ לֹא־ תֹאבַ֨ד תּוֹרָ֜ה מִכֹּהֵ֗ן וְעֵצָה֙ מֵֽחָכָ֔ם וְדָבָ֖ר מִנָּבִ֑יא לְכוּ֙ וְנַכֵּ֣הוּ בַלָּשׁ֔וֹן וְאַל־ נַקְשִׁ֖יבָה אֶל־ כָּל־ דְּבָרָֽיו׃

passages.text: Attend to me, O LORD. Hear what my accusers are saying!
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah is a prophet.
Jeremiah speaks to the LORD.
Jeremiah says, “LORD, listen to me.”
Jeremiah says, “Hear the words of those who accuse me.”
passages.original: הַקְשִׁ֥יבָה יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י וּשְׁמַ֖ע לְק֥וֹל יְרִיבָֽי׃

passages.text: Should good be repaid with evil? Yet they have dug a pit for me. Remember how I stood before You to speak good on their behalf, to turn Your wrath from them.
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah was a prophet.
People planned evil against Jeremiah.
Jeremiah had done good for them.
Jeremiah asked, “Should people repay good with evil?”
They dug a pit to trap Jeremiah.
Jeremiah spoke to God.
Jeremiah said, “Remember how I stood before You.”
Jeremiah spoke good things about the people to God.
Jeremiah tried to turn God’s anger away from them.
passages.original: הַיְשֻׁלַּ֤ם תַּֽחַת־ טוֹבָה֙ רָעָ֔ה כִּֽי־ כָר֥וּ שׁוּחָ֖ה לְנַפְשִׁ֑י זְכֹ֣ר׀ עָמְדִ֣י לְפָנֶ֗יךָ לְדַבֵּ֤ר עֲלֵיהֶם֙ טוֹבָ֔ה לְהָשִׁ֥יב אֶת־ חֲמָתְךָ֖ מֵהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Therefore, hand their children over to famine; pour out the power of the sword upon them. Let their wives become childless and widowed; let their husbands be slain by disease, their young men struck down by the sword in battle.
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD.
God is responding to the people who have done evil.
God says: Give their children to famine.
Let the sword destroy them.
Let their wives lose their children.
Let their wives become widows.
Let their husbands die by deadly sickness.
Let their young men die by the sword in battle.
passages.original: לָכֵן֩ תֵּ֨ן אֶת־ בְּנֵיהֶ֜ם לָרָעָ֗ב וְהַגִּרֵם֮ עַל־ יְדֵי־ חֶרֶב֒ וְתִֽהְיֶ֨נָה נְשֵׁיהֶ֤ם שַׁכֻּלוֹת֙ וְאַלְמָנ֔וֹת וְאַ֨נְשֵׁיהֶ֔ם יִֽהְי֖וּ הֲרֻ֣גֵי מָ֑וֶת בַּח֣וּרֵיהֶ֔ם מֻכֵּי־ חֶ֖רֶב בַּמִּלְחָמָֽה׃

passages.text: Let a cry be heard from their houses when You suddenly bring raiders against them, for they have dug a pit to capture me and have hidden snares for my feet.
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD.
God sees the actions of the people.
The people have done evil against God's servant.
They have dug a pit to trap me.
They have hidden snares for my feet.
You, LORD, will bring raiders against them suddenly.
A cry will be heard from their houses.
passages.original: תִּשָּׁמַ֤ע זְעָקָה֙ מִבָּ֣תֵּיהֶ֔ם כִּֽי־ תָבִ֧יא עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם גְּד֖וּד פִּתְאֹ֑ם כִּֽי־ כָר֤וּ שִׁיחָה לְלָכְדֵ֔נִי וּפַחִ֖ים טָמְנ֥וּ לְרַגְלָֽי׃

passages.text: But You, O LORD, know all their deadly plots against me. Do not wipe out their guilt or blot out their sin from Your sight. Let them be overthrown before You; deal with them in the time of Your anger.
passages.sermon:
The LORD knows everything.
The LORD knows all the plans of my enemies.
These people have made plans to kill me.
LORD, do not forgive their guilt.
Do not erase their sin from Your sight.
Let them stumble before You.
Act against them when You are angry.
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֣ה יְ֠הוָה יָדַ֜עְתָּ אֶֽת־ כָּל־ עֲצָתָ֤ם עָלַי֙ לַמָּ֔וֶת אַל־ תְּכַפֵּר֙ עַל־ עֲוֺנָ֔ם וְחַטָּאתָ֖ם מִלְּפָנֶ֣יךָ אַל־ תֶּ֑מְחִי וְהָיוּ מֻכְשָׁלִים֙ לְפָנֶ֔יךָ בְּעֵ֥ת אַפְּךָ֖ עֲשֵׂ֥ה בָהֶֽם׃ס
